# Cade Mini

> A small, durable coding agent built on one append-only session log.

# Cade Mini

<!-- source: README.md -->

# Cade Mini

Cade Mini is a standalone coding agent. It keeps one rule at the center of the
design:

> The session log is the source of truth. The model-visible history is a
> deterministic projection. Request construction only produces the current
> request.

The result is a small agent that can survive compaction, window changes, and
process restarts without inventing history.

- [CLI](cli.md) lists one-shot, REPL, session, and recovery commands.

## Built docs

The docs are Markdown-first. A small tool validates links and anchors, builds a
single-page site, and generates an `llms.txt` catalog for agents:

```bash
python -m cade_mini.docs check
python -m cade_mini.docs build
python -m cade_mini.docs llms --write
python -m cade_mini.docs catalogs --write
```

The generated site is [docs/index.html](index.html); the generated
catalogs are `docs/llms.txt`, `docs/llms-full.txt`, and the
config, event, and module pages under `design/`.

# Quickstart

<!-- source: quickstart.md -->

# Quickstart

Cade Mini requires Python 3.12 or newer. The repository uses `uv` for
development and for the `cade-mini` entry point.

## Install and authenticate

From the repository root:

```bash
uv sync --locked
uv run --locked cade-mini
```

On the first interactive launch without a project configuration, Cade Mini shows
an inline provider/model setup in the terminal's normal color scheme and
scrollback. Choose with ↑/↓, confirm with Enter, or cancel with Esc. The wizard
asks for a reasoning level when supported and securely masks API-key input.
Cancelling does not write a partial `cade-mini.json`.

Cade Mini owns its credential store at `~/.cade-mini/auth.json`. Log in with
Sign in with ChatGPT (SIWC) in a browser:

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini login
```

The browser flow registers Cade Mini on first use and reuses that registration
on later sign-ins. It stores a stable host ID at `~/.cade-mini/host.json`. SIWC
has no device-code flow. On a headless host, complete the login locally, copy
`auth.json`, and let the remote host create its own host ID on the next login.
Or use an API key.

For an OpenAI API key, use a hidden key prompt or set the environment variable:

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini login --provider openai
export OPENAI_API_KEY=...
uv run --locked cade-mini --provider openai --model gpt-5.5 "Review this project."
```

The default provider is `chatgpt`. Set `provider` and `model` in
`cade-mini.json` to choose other startup defaults. Cade Mini supports only the
OpenAI Responses protocol: `chatgpt` for ChatGPT plan usage and `openai`
for an API key. Mini does not read Cade's credentials, skills, or settings.

## Run one task

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini "Read README.md and explain the entry point in three bullets."
```

The same command can be written explicitly:

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini exec "Read README.md and explain the entry point."
```

Cade Mini runs in the current directory by default. Use `--project-root` to
point at another workspace.

## Choose a mode

- `act` is the default. Reads run directly; writes and shell commands ask.
- `build` allows structured writes and read-only shell commands. Mutating shell
  commands still ask.
- `plan` hides write and edit tools and denies mutations. Read-only shell
  commands are allowed.

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini --mode plan "Propose a fix for the failing test."
uv run --locked cade-mini --mode build "Fix the bug and run the test."
```

For non-interactive automation, `--yes` approves asks, and `--read-only` denies
writes and shell commands. Prefer rule-based allows over `--yes` for shared
repositories; see [Configuration](configuration.md).

## Continue work

Sessions live under `.cade-mini/sessions` by default.

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini --list-sessions
uv run --locked cade-mini --continue "What did you change?"
uv run --locked cade-mini --resume SESSION_ID "Continue the task."
```

Omitting the task starts the interactive REPL. See [CLI](cli.md) for all REPL
commands.

## Build the docs

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra docs
uv run --locked python -m cade_mini.docs check
uv run --locked python -m cade_mini.docs build
```

Open `docs/index.html`. The docs source is under `docs/`.

# CLI

<!-- source: cli.md -->

# CLI

The `cade-mini` entry point runs one task, starts an interactive TUI, or manages sessions.

```bash
cade-mini [TASK] [options]
cade-mini exec TASK [options]
```

`exec` is an explicit alias for a one-shot task. Without a task, `cade-mini`
starts the inline TUI on an interactive terminal. Use `--no-tui` for the
legacy REPL.

## Interactive terminal

The TUI uses an inline, colorized welcome page, an adaptive one-to-five-line
editor, a two-line status bar, searchable slash-command completion, native
terminal scrollback, streamed Markdown, tool/reasoning folding and
project/session/model selectors. A new project can be configured through an inline provider/model setup wizard
using the same terminal palette and keyboard controls, with no full-screen
modal. ChatGPT uses SIWC browser login and OpenAI uses a masked API-key input.
Esc cancels onboarding without writing project configuration. Existing login credentials remain in the Mini store.

- Enter sends a prompt; while busy, Enter queues, Alt+Enter steers, Ctrl+C cancels.
- Ctrl+J inserts a newline; Ctrl+O expands tool details (and approval previews);
  Ctrl+T expands model reasoning.
- PageUp/PageDown scroll a long approval preview; Enter accepts the selected
  decision; Esc denies it.
- / commands, @file references, $skills, !shell, and model selection have
  in-terminal completion.
- Shift+Tab changes mode; Ctrl+D twice exits on an empty prompt. Ctrl+Q exits.
- /btw QUESTION asks an isolated streaming side question without logging it.
- Ctrl+K opens the searchable command palette, Ctrl+P the model selector, and
  Ctrl+G the session selector. Press ? with an empty prompt for keyboard help.
- Session, model, configuration and tool selectors support fuzzy search;
  use ↑/↓ and Enter, Tab to focus the list, Esc to close.
- The model selector includes a custom model ID entry.
- Consecutive completed read/search tool calls are grouped in compact view;
  Ctrl+O expands their individual calls, results and edit diffs.
- When the model invokes `question`, the TUI collects single choices, multiple
  choices or a free-text answer without restarting the agent. Ctrl+J inserts a
  newline in a free-text answer; Enter submits it.
- An existing workspace with missing or expired credentials still opens the TUI
  in an explicit sign-in-required state; use `/login` to reconnect. One-shot
  tasks keep their fail-fast authentication behavior.
- `/tool NAME JSON` runs one tool interactively with the same hooks, approvals,
  and folded output as model-initiated tools.

A task or `exec TASK` continues to run once and exit, without opening the TUI.

## Login

```bash
cade-mini login
cade-mini login --provider openai
```

`--provider` defaults to `chatgpt`, which uses Sign in with ChatGPT (SIWC)
in a browser. `openai` uses `api_key` with a hidden input prompt. Credentials
are stored in `~/.cade-mini/auth.json`; the stable SIWC host ID is stored in
`~/.cade-mini/host.json`. Login does not change project provider or model
settings. Cade Mini supports only the OpenAI Responses protocol.

## One-shot options

- `--project-root PATH` sets the workspace. The default is the current
  directory.
- `--config PATH` selects a config file. The default is
  `<project-root>/cade-mini.json`. In the TUI, `/config` edits this same file
  rather than silently writing the default.
- `--provider NAME`, `--model NAME`, and `--effort EFFORT` override provider
  defaults.
- `--mode plan|build|act` selects the execution mode.
- `--read-only` / `--no-read-only` denies or permits writes and shell commands.
- `--yes` approves asks. Use it only in trusted, non-interactive contexts.
- `--auto-review` / `--no-auto-review` lets the model review ask-level calls.
- `--max-steps N` bounds model steps.
- `--context-window N` overrides the model context window.
- `--json` emits JSONL events for a one-shot task.
- `--tui` / `--no-tui` forces or disables the inline interactive terminal.
- `--steer TEXT` injects guidance at the next model step; repeatable.
- `--queue TEXT` queues a REPL task to run after the current task; repeatable.

## Sessions

- `--list-sessions` prints ID, update time, and title, then exits.
- `--continue` resumes the latest session in the project.
- `--resume` resumes the latest session; `--resume ID` resumes a specific one.
- `--sessions-dir PATH` changes the session directory. A relative path is
  resolved against the project root.
- `--undo` restores the latest file snapshot and exits without contacting a
  provider.

`--continue` and `--resume` cannot be combined.

## Goals

- `--goal TEXT` sets the workspace goal before running.

## Interactive commands (TUI)

Slash commands are completed while typing. Enter accepts a completion; the
terminal also shows the selected command's argument hint. Commands that require
a choice open an in-terminal selector where available.

| Area | Commands |
|---|---|
| Sessions | `/new`, `/clear`, `/continue`, `/resume [ID]`, `/sessions`, `/rename TITLE` |
| History | `/fork [turn|ID]`, `/clone`, `/tree [ID]`, `/rewind [N]`, `/undo [N|--list]`, `/compact`, `/rollover [--force]` |
| Models | `/model [provider/]model`, `/effort [level]`, `/thinking [on|off]`, `/context-window [size|default]`, `/context` |
| Work | `/mode [act|build|plan]`, `/queue [followup|steer|interrupt|task]`, `/steer TEXT`, `/stop`, `/btw QUESTION`, `/goal [text|pause|resume|done|clear]` |
| Connections | `/login [provider]`, `/connect [provider]`, `/logout [provider]`, `/auth [status|login|logout]` |
| Settings | `/config [setting[=value]]`, `/permissions [list|clear]`, `/hooks`, `/mcp`, `/tool [list|NAME JSON]`, `/skill [name]`, `/memory` |
| Help and exit | `/help`, `/exit`, `/quit` |

`/revert` aliases `/undo`, and `/new-context` aliases `/rollover`.
`/fork`, `/resume`, `/model`, `/effort`, `/mode`, `/permissions`,
`/config`, `/login`, `/logout`, `/skill`, and `/tool` offer native
selection when called without arguments.

`/rollover` requires a workspace `NOTE.md` with a handoff note. The
`--force` argument skips that guard. `/undo` restores completed, still-safe
file snapshots; `--list` only lists them. Changes to `/config` are saved
atomically and become effective on the next launch.

The line-oriented `--no-tui` REPL retains its own input handling and
command support.

## Interactive input

- `@path` attaches a workspace file to the task.
- `$skill` loads a skill body into the task.
- `!command` runs a shell command without contacting the model. Permission
  checks still apply.

```text
Review @src/cade_mini/core/loop.py and use $review-only
!git status
```

During a task, the REPL keeps reading input:

- `/steer TEXT` appends guidance at the next model step.
- `/queue TEXT` runs TEXT after the current task.
- `/stop` cancels at the next safe point.
- Other text is queued as a follow-up task.

Steering is applied between steps, not inside a provider stream or a running
tool. See [Steering and queueing](design/steering-queue.md).

## Exit codes

- `0`: the run completed.
- `1`: the run ended without completion, or no snapshot was available for
  `--undo`.
- `2`: argument, configuration, or startup error.
- `130`: login was cancelled.

## Examples

```bash
cade-mini --list-sessions
cade-mini --continue "Summarize the current state."
cade-mini --undo
cade-mini --mode plan "Find the smallest fix for the failing test."
cade-mini --mode build --yes "Fix the test and run pytest."
```

# Configuration

<!-- source: configuration.md -->

# Configuration

Cade Mini reads `<project-root>/cade-mini.json` by default. Use `--config PATH`
to select another file. Command-line options override the file; the file
overrides built-in defaults.

The file is strict: unknown keys and invalid values are rejected instead of
silently ignored.

## Example

```json
{
  "provider": "chatgpt",
  "model": "gpt-5.6-luna",
  "reasoning_effort": "high",
  "context_window": 128000,
  "max_steps": 30,
  "sessions_dir": ".cade-mini/sessions",
  "mode": "act",
  "read_only": false,
  "instructions": true,
  "note": true,
  "memory": true,
  "auto_review": false,
  "prompt_modules": ["identity", "tool_discipline", "working_note", "environment"],
  "rules": [
    {
      "tool": "bash",
      "command_prefix": "git status",
      "decision": "allow"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Fields

- `provider`, `model`: provider name and model identifier. Use `chatgpt`
  for ChatGPT plan usage (Sign in with ChatGPT) or `openai` for an OpenAI API
  key. The CLI flags override both.
- `reasoning_effort`: provider reasoning effort. The CLI flag is `--effort`.
- `context_window`: model context window in tokens.
- `max_steps`: maximum model steps in one run.
- `sessions_dir`: session directory. Relative paths resolve against the project
  root.
- `mode`: `plan`, `build`, or `act`.
- `read_only`: deny writes and shell commands.
- `instructions`: load `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` into request context.
- `note`: load `NOTE.md` working state.
- `memory`: load `MEMORY.md` durable facts.
- `auto_review`: let the model review ask-level tool calls. Default is false.
- `prompt_modules`: system prompt modules. Available names are `identity`,
  `tool_discipline`, `working_note`, and `environment`.

## Rules

Rules are evaluated last match first. A rule matches a tool name or `*`, and
optionally a path or command prefix. `decision` is `allow`, `deny`, or `ask`.

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {"tool": "bash", "command_prefix": "git", "decision": "deny"},
    {"tool": "bash", "command_prefix": "git status", "decision": "allow"},
    {"tool": "write", "path_prefix": "docs/", "decision": "allow"}
  ]
}
```

Hard boundaries win over rules: a path outside the workspace is denied even if a
rule allows the tool. `read_only` also wins over grants and rules.

## Hooks

Hooks run shell commands around tools. A non-zero `before_tool` hook denies the
call.

```json
{
  "hooks": [
    {
      "event": "before_tool",
      "command": "python tools/check_tool.py",
      "matcher": "bash",
      "timeout_ms": 10000
    }
  ]
}
```

`event` is `before_tool` or `after_tool`. `matcher` is a tool name, a prefix
ending in `*`, or omitted for all tools. Hooks receive `CADE_HOOK_EVENT`,
`CADE_TOOL_NAME`, `CADE_TOOL_ARGS`, and `CADE_TOOL_RESULT` in the environment.

## MCP servers

MCP servers use stdio and keep one persistent connection per server.

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": {
    "files": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["mcp_server.py"],
      "cwd": ".",
      "timeout_ms": 30000,
      "env": {"LOG_LEVEL": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

Discovered tools are exposed as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. They ask by default,
are denied in plan mode and read-only mode, and can be allowed by a rule.

# Architecture

<!-- source: architecture.md -->

# Architecture

Cade Mini is a standalone coding agent in `src/cade_mini/`. It uses a pipeline
with four stages. Each stage has one owner and one direction of data flow.

```text
Session log -> Conversation projection -> Request -> Run
```

## Session log

`SessionLog` is an append-only JSONL file. Each entry has an ID, timestamp,
type, parent ID, and data. The active branch ends at the latest entry. A tree is
possible, but the loop follows one branch.

The log stores facts:

- `system`, `user`, `assistant`, and `tool_result` are model-visible facts.
- `compaction` records a summary and `first_kept_id`.
- `window` records a new context start and an optional handoff.
- `request`, `run`, and `attempt` are audit facts. They never become
  conversation messages.

The schema is closed and versioned. See [Session log schema](reference/session-schema.md).

## Projection

`project(entries)` is a pure function. It reads the branch and produces the
deterministic conversation projection:

1. Take the latest system message.
2. Apply the latest window start.
3. Apply the latest compaction summary.
4. Keep retained user, assistant, and tool-result messages.
5. Pair tool calls with tool results; insert a synthetic interrupted result at
   the tail when the log ends mid-call.

No projection step writes to the log. Replaying the same entries always
produces the same conversation.

## Request

`build(conversation, tools, budget, context)` admits messages into the current
model window. It:

- joins request-only context such as instructions, skill catalog, NOTE, memory,
  and goal;
- preserves every projected message and tool result;
- checks the complete request against the input budget;
- converts the result to provider wire format;
- returns a `Request` with a `BuildReport`.

Admission does not mutate the conversation and does not write facts. Only
compaction and window events change the visible history. An over-budget request
is rejected rather than silently truncated.

## Run

Before appending a new user fact, `run()` persists interrupted results for
unfinished tool calls. It does not repeat tools whose outcome is unknown.
It then calls the provider, appends assistant and tool-result facts, and executes
tools. It is the only stage that writes during a turn. Compaction and window
fallback are decisions expressed as new log facts.

## Package map

- `core/types.py`: log, message, block, and error types.
- `core/events.py`: strict v2 event payload validation.
- `core/log.py`: append, lock, tail repair, session listing, copy/fork.
- `core/projection.py`: deterministic conversation projection.
- `core/request.py`: budget, admission, wire conversion.
- `core/loop.py`: provider stream, tool execution, retries, facts.
- `core/compaction.py` and `core/window.py`: context reduction decisions.
- `tools/workspace.py`, `tools/history.py`: workspace tools and evidence
  retrieval.
- `safety/policy.py`, `safety/shell.py`, `safety/grants.py`,
  `safety/approval.py`, `safety/review.py`: permissions and approvals.
- `extensions/skills.py`, `extensions/memory.py`, `extensions/hooks.py`,
  `extensions/mcp.py`, `extensions/subagents.py`, `extensions/snapshots.py`,
  `extensions/goal.py`: add-ons and durable host state.
- `app/config.py`, `app/provider.py`, `app/auth.py`, `app/prompts.py`,
  `app/instructions.py`, `app/note.py`: startup and request context.
- `hosts/cli.py`, `docs.py`: hosts and documentation.

Mini owns `cade_mini.ai` and `cade_mini.execution_env` as lower layers for
provider protocols and local process execution. It does not depend on the
separate Cade project. `test_mini_boundary.py` rejects old Cade imports and
application dependencies in these lower layers. There are no top-level
re-exports; import the owning submodule directly.

## Lower layers and state

`ai/` owns provider protocols, streaming adapters, model metadata, and OAuth.
`execution_env/` owns local process execution and output capture. Neither layer
imports application or host modules. The AI layer supports only the OpenAI
Responses protocol, as recorded in [decision 0007](decisions/0007-responses-only-provider.md),
and uses Sign in with ChatGPT for plan usage, as recorded in
[decision 0008](decisions/0008-siwc-login.md).
Mini has no OS sandbox; shell execution uses local host permissions.

Credentials and user skills use `~/.cade-mini/`. The SIWC host ID lives in
`~/.cade-mini/host.json`. Sessions, snapshots, goals,
and project skills use `<workspace>/.cade-mini/`. Project settings live in
`cade-mini.json`. Mini does not discover old Cade state.

See the [code map](design/code-map.md) and
[persistence catalog](design/persistence-catalog.md) for implementation locations
and durable state ownership.

## Why the split

The split prevents a common failure: the request builder starts hiding
messages, then the history rewrite becomes the only copy of what happened. Mini
keeps the original facts and lets the projection and admission be replaced
without losing history.

# Sessions and context

<!-- source: sessions-context.md -->

# Sessions and context

A session is an append-only JSONL file under `.cade-mini/sessions` by default.
The file name is `session-<id>.jsonl`. The session title is derived from the
first user message; no extra event type is needed.

## Resume

```bash
cade-mini --list-sessions
cade-mini --continue "Continue where we stopped."
cade-mini --resume SESSION_ID "Explain the current state."
```

`--continue` and `--resume` open the latest or a specific session. Existing
sessions keep their original system fact; a new `cade-mini.json` does not rewrite
history. If a resumed session has no system entry, the current prompt is added.

## Fork, clone, tree, and rewind

- `/clone` copies the active branch into a new session.
- `/fork [N|ENTRY]` copies history before a user turn (default: latest) into a
  new session and prints the forked input.
- `/tree` lists entries; `*` marks the active branch.
- `/rewind [N]` creates a new session without the latest N user turns.
- `/undo [N]` restores the latest N file snapshots.

These operations create new sessions; they do not rewrite the original file.
Compaction and window references are remapped when entries are copied.

## Compaction

When the full conversation exceeds the input budget, `Compactor`:

1. Selects a cut at a visible user boundary.
2. Sends the older messages to the provider for a summary.
3. Appends a `compaction` fact with the summary and `first_kept_id`.
4. Reprojects the conversation as the latest system, summary, and retained tail.

Compaction is iterative: a prior summary is serialized as `PRIOR SUMMARY` and
can be summarized again. The original user, assistant, and tool-result facts
remain in the log.

## Request admission

Request construction preserves the entire projection, including tool outputs.
Only logged compaction and window events reduce visible history. If the request
still exceeds the budget after these steps, the loop returns `context_error`
without sending it to the provider. Use the `history` tool to retrieve evidence
outside the current context.

## Windows

A `window` fact starts a new context at a user entry and may include a handoff.
The CLI can start one explicitly with `/new-context`. If compaction cannot bring
a request under budget, the loop can append an automatic window with a fixed
handoff that points to `NOTE.md` and the history tool.

## History tool

`history` accepts one of:

- `query`: case-insensitive search over the branch, returning entry IDs and
  snippets.
- `entry_id`: exact content of one log entry.
- `call_id`: exact tool result for one call.

Exact content is capped. Search results are capped and point back to entry IDs.

## Request context order

For each task the request contains:

1. The system message.
2. Project instructions from `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or their variants.
3. The skill catalog.
4. `NOTE.md` working state.
5. `MEMORY.md` durable facts.
6. An active goal.

Items 2-6 are request-only context. They are recorded in the request audit but
never become conversation facts. See [Architecture](architecture.md) and the
[design](history/design-proposal.md).

# How Cade Mini works

<!-- source: design/how-it-works.md -->

# How Cade Mini works

Cade Mini coordinates one model request at a time, executes the requested tools,
and records every durable fact in a session log.

## One run

A submitted task is appended as a `user` fact. Cade Mini projects the active
branch, builds a request for the current budget, and sends it to the provider.
The provider streams text and tool calls. The loop records the assistant
message, executes each tool call, and records a tool result. If the model needs
another request, the loop starts another step; otherwise the run ends.

A step is one request plus the tools caused by its response. A run can contain
many steps. The loop stops on completion, a step limit, context exhaustion,
cancellation, or a provider error.

## Context

The projection supplies conversation history. Request-only context supplies
project instructions, the skill catalog, `NOTE.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and an active
goal. Tool results are pruned when they no longer fit; the history tool can read
the original facts.

Compaction adds a summary fact and keeps a recent tail. A window moves the
context start forward and may include a handoff. Neither operation rewrites the
original messages.

## Sessions

Sessions are JSONL files under `.cade-mini/sessions`. Entries have IDs and parent
IDs, so a session can form a tree; the active branch ends at the latest entry.
Resuming opens the same file and appends new facts.

## Interfaces

The terminal host runs one task or a REPL. It calls the same loop and shares
policy, tools, and session storage with every other entry path.

## Extensions

Skills add on-demand instructions. Memory adds durable facts. Hooks run shell
commands around tools. MCP adds remote tools. Subagents run an independent child
session. Each extension is a narrow adapter over the loop, not a change to the
session schema.

## Trust and permissions

Every tool call passes through a policy. Modes, static rules, session grants,
shell classification, and approvals decide whether a call runs. Cade Mini has
no OS sandbox; the path boundary, mode, shell classification, and approvals are
the active safety layer.

See [Architecture](../architecture.md) for the invariant and
[Capability seams](capability-seams.md) for the contracts.

# Code map

<!-- source: design/code-map.md -->

# Code map

Cade Mini is an independent project. The `cade-mini` distribution installs the
`cade_mini` package and the `cade-mini` command. It does not install or depend
on Cade.

## Package layout

```text
src/cade_mini/
  ai/             provider adapters, events, auth protocols, models
  execution_env/  local subprocess execution and output capture
  core/           log, projection, request, loop, compaction, window
  tools/          workspace actions and history retrieval
  safety/         policy, shell analysis, grants, approval, review
  extensions/     skills, memory, hooks, mcp, subagents, snapshots, goal
  app/            config, provider assembly, credentials, request context
  hosts/          cli, auth
  docs.py
  __main__.py
tests/            regression and integration tests
```

Provider and execution modules originated in Cade and are now owned and
maintained here. Mini includes only the process execution code it uses, not
Cade's filesystem or Linux sandbox implementation. Mini has no OS sandbox.

## Entry points

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini
uv run --locked cade-mini exec "Fix the failing test."
uv run --locked python -m cade_mini
uv run --locked cade-mini login
```

The console script and Python module call `cade_mini.hosts.cli:main`. Login
is handled by `cade_mini.hosts.auth`. Credentials and user skills live under
`~/.cade-mini/`. Project sessions and other state live under `.cade-mini/`.
No old Cade directories or commands are used.

## Import direction

- `ai` and `execution_env` do not import application or host modules.
- `core` imports core types and AI protocols.
- `tools`, `safety`, and `extensions` connect actions and policies to the core.
- `app` owns startup settings, credential persistence, and request context.
- `hosts` assemble these components and own user interaction.

`tests/test_mini_boundary.py` rejects imports from the old `cade` namespace
and application imports in the lower layers. The package root has no public
re-exports; import the owning submodule directly.

See [Architecture](../architecture.md),
[How Cade Mini works](how-it-works.md), and
[Capability seams](capability-seams.md) for runtime contracts.

# Relationship to Cade

<!-- source: design/cade-comparison.md -->

# Relationship to Cade

Cade and Cade Mini are separate projects. This repository develops, tests, and
releases only Cade Mini. It does not provide compatibility with Cade's Python
package, commands, settings, credentials, or session formats.

Mini originated as a log-first implementation alongside Cade. Its provider
adapters and process execution code were brought into the `cade_mini` package
when it became independent. They are no longer shared runtime dependencies.

## Mini's product boundary

Mini provides a terminal REPL and one-shot execution. Its core separates
append-only session facts, deterministic projection, request admission, and the
run loop.

Intentional limits include:

- No full-screen TUI, plugin runtime, RPC, or SDK.
- No artifact store or parallel tool scheduler.
- No permanent approval grants; durable rules belong in project config.
- No OS sandbox; permissions and shell classification are application checks.

The [historical parity acceptance](../parity.md) records workflows tested
before separation. It is not a promise of future feature parity. See the
[code map](code-map.md) for the current package and ownership boundaries.

# Capability seams

<!-- source: design/capability-seams.md -->

# Capability seams

Cade Mini keeps a small number of explicit contracts. A seam is a place where an
implementation can be replaced without changing the session schema or the loop.

| Seam | Contract | Implementations | Main consumers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Provider | `loop.Provider` streaming events | OpenAI Responses, ChatGPT plan (SIWC) | Loop, compaction, auto-review |
| Tool | `loop.Tool` name, description, parameters, execute | Workspace tools, history, skill, memory, goal, subagent, MCP | Loop |
| Policy | `loop.Policy.check` returns allow, deny, or ask | `WorkspacePolicy` | Loop |
| Approval | Callable returning bool or awaitable bool | `SessionApprover`, `AutoReviewer` | Loop |
| Hooks | `loop.Hooks.before/after` | `HookRunner` | Loop |
| Compaction | `Compactor(log, budget)` | LLM summary compactor | Loop |
| Session store | `SessionLog` append, branch, open | File-backed JSONL log | Every layer above it |
| Recovery | `SnapshotStore` capture and undo | File snapshot store | Tools, CLI |
| Host | A task runner over the loop | CLI | Users |

## Provider

The loop needs a streaming event source: text deltas, tool calls, a final
message, usage, and failures. A provider owns wire conversion and replay state.
Cade Mini does not depend on provider-specific message types above this seam.

## Tool

A tool declares a JSON schema and an async `execute`. A tool result is content,
an error flag, and optional metadata. Tools do not write the session log; the
loop records their results.

## Policy and approval

Policy returns a decision, not an execution. Approval is only consulted for
`ask`. A denial becomes a tool error fact, so the model can recover. Keeping
these separate lets the host choose a TTY prompt, a model reviewer, or a
non-interactive denial.

## Hooks

Hooks observe and can veto a tool call without changing the policy result. A
`before_tool` failure is a denial; `after_tool` failure is ignored. Hooks are
trusted configuration, not sandboxed code.

## Stores

`SessionLog` is the durable history. `SnapshotStore`, `GoalStore`, and the
memory and NOTE files are host state, not session facts. Treating them as
separate stores keeps the schema closed while allowing recovery and long-term
state.

## Host

A host owns presentation, input, and the event loop boundary. It does not own
the agent loop or the schema. The CLI renders events and runs tasks without
changing either.

## Tests as contracts

Each seam has a focused test module. `test_mini_boundary.py` enforces the import
firewall, so a seam cannot quietly become a dependency on the Cade product
layers.

# Event model

<!-- source: design/event-model.md -->

# Event model

A session is a tree of entries, not a message array. Entry types fall into two
groups.

## Model-visible facts

These entries project into the conversation:

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Base system prompt; the latest one wins |
| `user` | User task or steering input |
| `assistant` | Text and tool calls produced by one model response |
| `tool_result` | Result paired to a tool call |
| `compaction` | Summary plus `first_kept_id`; shadows older entries |
| `window` | New context start plus optional handoff |

`compaction` and `window` also carry projections of their own: a summary
message. The original entries remain readable by the history tool.

## Audit facts

These entries never project:

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `meta` | Session creation metadata |
| `request` | Provider, model, context, digests, estimated tokens, dropped evidence |
| `attempt` | One provider attempt, including failures and retries |
| `run` | Termination, steps, usage, error |

Audit facts make the request reproducible without turning diagnostics into
conversation. A failed run therefore cannot fabricate an assistant message.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  log[Session log] --> project[Projection]
  project --> conversation[Conversation]
  conversation --> request[Request build]
  request --> provider[Provider stream]
  provider --> facts[Assistant and tool-result facts]
  facts --> log
  request --> audit[request fact]
  provider --> attempts[attempt facts]
  facts --> run[run fact]
```

The loop appends the user fact before the first request. Each step appends one
assistant fact and zero or more tool-result facts. A run appends exactly one
`run` fact.

## Ordering and pairing

A tool result follows its assistant tool call. Projection rejects an orphan
result or a duplicate result. If the branch ends after a tool call without a
result, projection inserts a synthetic interrupted result at the tail so the
request remains protocol-valid.

## Compaction and windows

A compaction cuts at a user boundary. Its summary message appears first in the
retained context. A window discards earlier entries and may insert a handoff.
Only the latest cut applies. Compaction is preferred; a window is a fallback
when a summary cannot fit.

## Schema authority

The closed schema is in [Session log schema](../reference/session-schema.md). The
generated [event catalog](event-catalog.md) lists the current event types from
code.

# Tool execution

<!-- source: design/tool-execution.md -->

# Tool execution

Every tool call follows the same pipeline. Policy and approval decide whether a
call may run; hooks can stop it; the loop owns execution and recording.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  call[Tool call] --> policy[Policy decision]
  policy -->|deny| denied[Denied tool result]
  policy -->|ask| approval[Approval]
  approval -->|deny| denied
  approval -->|allow| before[before_tool hooks]
  policy -->|allow| before
  before -->|deny| hookdenied[Hook-denied result]
  before -->|allow| execute[Execute tool]
  execute --> after[after_tool hooks]
  execute --> result[Tool result]
  result --> log[Append fact]
  denied --> log
  hookdenied --> log
```

## Order

1. The model returns a tool call with an ID and arguments.
2. Policy checks tool name, path, mode, rules, grants, and shell classification.
3. An `ask` decision is resolved by the host: TTY prompt, `--yes`, auto-review,
   or denial.
4. `before_tool` hooks run. A non-zero exit denies the call.
5. The tool executes with a timeout and cancellation token.
6. The result is truncated, appended as a `tool_result` fact, and rendered.
7. `after_tool` hooks run and their output is ignored.

## Denials and errors

A denied call is not an exception. It becomes an error tool result so the model
can adapt. Unknown tools, malformed arguments, timeouts, and thrown exceptions
also become error results. A cancellation appends interrupted results for any
remaining calls before the run terminates.

## Hooks

Hooks receive the tool name, JSON arguments, and the result for `after_tool`.
They run with the workspace as the current directory. A hook timeout is a
denial or a silently ignored observer, never an unbounded wait.

## Evidence retention

Tool results are facts. Request admission can replace old bodies with a
reference that names the `call_id`. The history tool retrieves the exact result
from the branch, so pruning does not destroy evidence.

## Tests

- `test_mini_loop.py` covers approval, errors, timeouts, cancellation, retries,
  and window fallback.
- `test_mini_hooks.py` covers allow, deny, and after-hook execution.
- `test_mini_policy.py` covers modes, rules, grants, and boundaries.

See [Tools and security](../tools-security.md) for user-facing behavior.

# Tool catalog

<!-- source: design/tool-catalog.md -->

# Tool catalog

The built-in tool surface. MCP tools are discovered at startup and named
`mcp__<server>__<tool>`; their parameters come from the server.

| Tool | Parameters | Side effect | Default policy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `read` | `path`, `offset`, `limit` | None | Allow inside workspace |
| `write` | `path`, `content` | Creates or replaces a file; snapshot first | Ask in act, allow in build |
| `edit` | `path`, `old`, `new` | Replaces one occurrence; snapshot first | Ask in act, allow in build |
| `glob` | `pattern`, `path` | None | Allow |
| `grep` | `pattern`, `path`, `include` | None | Allow |
| `bash` | `command`, `workdir`, `timeout_ms` | Arbitrary process; snapshot common mutations | Ask except read-only shell |
| `history` | `query`, `entry_id`, `call_id`, `limit` | None | Allow |
| `skill` | `name` | None; loads a skill body | Allow |
| `memory` | `text` | Appends to `MEMORY.md` | Allow; denied read-only |
| `goal` | `action`, `objective` | Updates `.cade-mini/goal.json` | Allow |
| `subagent` | `prompt`, `description` | Creates a child session | Allow; hidden in plan |
| `delegate` | `prompt` or `tasks`, `mode`, `description` | Creates one or more child sessions | Allow |
| `mcp__*` | Server-defined | Remote side effects | Ask; denied plan and read-only |

## Reading the table

- "Side effect" is what the tool can change, not what it always changes.
- `write` and `edit` fail closed if the snapshot cannot be taken.
- `bash` read-only classification is conservative; unknown commands ask in
  build and act and are denied in plan.
- MCP tools are dynamic. A rule can allow a specific tool; the default is ask.

## Parameters

The authoritative JSON schemas are built into each tool. This table is a
navigation aid; when it disagrees with the tool schema, the schema wins.

## Related

- [Tools and security](../tools-security.md)
- [Tool execution](tool-execution.md)
- [Configuration catalog](config-catalog.md)

# MCP reference servers

<!-- source: design/mcp-reference.md -->

# MCP reference servers

Cade Mini implements stdio `initialize`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call` with a
persistent connection per server. That is enough for the reference servers that
expose tools.

## Verified servers

| Server | Command | Verified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Filesystem | `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem <dir>` | Discovery and `read_text_file` |
| Memory | `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory` | Discovery of entity tools |
| Sequential Thinking | `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking` | Discovery of `sequentialthinking` |
| Time | `uvx mcp-server-time` | Discovery and `get_current_time` |
| Fetch | `uvx mcp-server-fetch` | Server starts and lists tools |

On Windows, run npm servers through `cmd /c`:

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": {
    "time": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-server-time"]
    },
    "fs": {
      "command": "cmd",
      "args": [
        "/c", "npx", "-y",
        "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem",
        "C:/path/to/workspace"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

On POSIX use `npx` directly. The Git server needs its repository flag, for
example `--repository <path>`; pass the exact arguments the server expects.

## Capability boundary

The reference servers above are tool servers. Cade Mini does not implement MCP
resources, prompts, sampling, or server-initiated requests. A server that relies
on those features will start but expose only its tools.

## Policy

MCP tools are named `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. They ask by default, are denied in
plan mode and with `--read-only`, and can be allowed by a rule:

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {"tool": "mcp__time__get_current_time", "decision": "allow"}
  ]
}
```

## Verify

```bash
cade-mini --mode build "Use the time MCP tool to get the current time in Asia/Singapore."
```

The log records a `tool_result` with the server's text content. A server process
is closed when Cade Mini exits.

## Related

- [Configuration](../configuration.md)
- [Hooks, MCP, and subagents](../hooks-mcp-subagents.md)
- [Custom MCP server](../cookbook/custom-mcp.md)

# Steering and queueing

<!-- source: design/steering-queue.md -->

# Steering and queueing

Cade Mini's REPL can read input while a task is running. The host does not block
the terminal on `_run_task`.

## Why the old REPL blocked

The first REPL called `input()` in the main thread and then ran the async loop
with `asyncio.run`. While that call was active, the terminal was not read, so
`/steer` and `/queue` could only affect the next task.

## Current design

```text
stdin
  |
  v
_InputPump thread  -- _Line -->  event queue
                                  |
task thread  -- _ApprovalRequest / _TaskDone --> event queue
                                  |
                                  v
                         REPL main thread
```

- `_InputPump` reads one line at a time and never calls the model.
- `_run_task` runs in a worker thread with its own `asyncio` event loop.
- The REPL main thread owns the event queue and the session state.
- `_HostApprover` sends `_ApprovalRequest` to the main thread and waits. The
  main thread reads the answer from the same input pump, so approvals do not
  compete with a second `input()`.
- `!command` runs in the main thread and uses `_ConsoleApprover`, which reads
  the answer directly from the event queue.

## Commands during a run

| Input | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `/steer TEXT` | Append guidance at the next model step |
| `/queue TEXT` | Run TEXT as a new task after the current task |
| `/stop` or `/cancel` | Cancel the current task at the next safe point |
| other text | Same as `/queue`: run it after the current task |
| `/exit` | Cancel, wait for the task to settle, then exit |

`/steer` is not a prompt injection into a running provider request. The loop
checks the steering queue before each step, appends a `user` fact with
`source: runtime`, and builds the next request from the projection. This keeps
the session log as the source of truth.

## Queue semantics

- A queued task starts automatically when the current task reaches a terminal
  state.
- Queue order is FIFO.
- A queued task runs in the same session; it is not a fork.
- `/fork`, `/clone`, `/rewind`, and session commands are main-thread commands.
  They are only handled when no task is active. During a run they are treated as
  queued text; finish or stop the run first.

## Limits

- Tools already executing are not killed. `/stop` takes effect at the next
  cancellation check.
- The input pump uses plain `input()`, not a full line editor. Editing,
  history, and completion are terminal features.
- Approval answers are read as the next line. Do not type a task while an
  approval prompt is waiting; it is consumed as the answer.
- The one-shot `--steer` flag seeds guidance before the first step. It is not a
  substitute for `/steer` during a run.

## Tests

- `test_live_input_handles_steer_and_queue`
- `test_live_input_is_read_while_worker_is_running`
- `test_mid_run_steer_reaches_the_next_provider_request`
- `test_repl_reads_steer_while_a_bash_tool_is_running`
- `test_host_approver_routes_through_events`
- `test_live_input_can_stop_the_task`

The end-to-end test blocks a tool until the host delivers `/steer`, then checks
that the next provider request contains the steering fact.

# Persistence catalog

<!-- source: design/persistence-catalog.md -->

# Persistence catalog

Cade Mini separates durable history from host state. The session log is the
authority for what the model saw and what happened; the other stores have
narrower jobs.

| Artifact | Default location | Owner | Lifetime | Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Session log | `.cade-mini/sessions/session-*.jsonl` | `SessionLog` | Project | Write v2; read v1/v2 |
| Snapshots | `.cade-mini/snapshots/` | `SnapshotStore` | Project | Local index |
| Goal | `.cade-mini/goal.json` | `GoalStore` | Project | One object |
| Working note | `NOTE.md` | Project | Project | Markdown |
| Memory | `MEMORY.md` | `MemoryTool` | Project | Markdown |
| Instructions | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, overrides | Project | Project | Markdown |
| Skills | `~/.cade-mini/skills`, `.cade-mini/skills` | Discovery | User or project | `SKILL.md` |
| Config | `cade-mini.json` | `MiniConfig` | Project | Pydantic, strict |
| Credentials | `~/.cade-mini/auth.json` | `JsonCredentialStore` | User | Provider credentials |
| SIWC host ID | `~/.cade-mini/host.json` | `load_or_create_host_id` | User | Stable agent host identifier |
| Docs site | `docs/index.html` | Docs tool | Repository | Generated |
| LLM catalogs | `docs/llms*.txt` | Docs tool | Repository | Generated |

## The session log

The log is append-only and versioned. It stores model-visible facts and audit
facts in one tree. It is the only artifact needed to reconstruct the
conversation. Compaction and windows are log entries, not rewrites.

## Snapshots

Snapshots are an undo journal for file changes. They cover `write`, `edit`, and
common single-command shell mutations. Format v2 uses an atomically replaced
JSONL index, immutable before/after records, and content-addressed original blobs.
See [Snapshots and goals](../snapshots-goals.md) for conflict and legacy behavior.
Snapshots are not part of the session branch.

## Goals and notes

A goal is one objective with an active or done status. `NOTE.md` is working
state that is included in every request and summarized during compaction.
`MEMORY.md` is durable project knowledge. These files are intentionally plain:
they can be edited by hand and inspected with ordinary tools.

## Generated artifacts

The docs site, `llms.txt`, and `llms-full.txt` are generated from Markdown and
`docs.json`. They are checked for freshness; do not edit the HTML by hand.

## What is not persisted

- Request-only context is recorded in the request audit, not as messages.
- Grants last for the process; durable policy belongs in config rules.
- Approval prompts and TUI state are host state.
- Provider replay payloads live inside the assistant fact that produced them.

See [Session log schema](../reference/session-schema.md) for field-level detail and
[Change policy](../persistence/change-policy.md) for schema changes.

# Glossary

<!-- source: design/glossary.md -->

# Glossary

One canonical term per concept. Links point to the owning page.

## session log

The append-only JSONL file that records facts. It is the source of truth for the
active branch. See [Log](../subsystems/log.md).

## branch

A path through the entry tree. The active branch ends at the latest entry and
supplies the projection.

## projection

The deterministic conversation produced from a branch. It applies the latest
system, compaction, and window cuts, then pairs tool calls with results. See
[Projection and request](../subsystems/projection-request.md).

## request

The admitted, provider-ready form of a conversation for one model call. It
includes tools, budget, and request-only context. A request is not a fact and is
never projected.

## run

One invocation of the loop over a task. A run contains one or more steps and
ends with a `run` fact.

## step

One model request plus the tool calls caused by its response.

## tool result

The recorded output of one tool call, paired by call ID. It is a fact.

## compaction

A fact that adds a summary and a `first_kept_id`. It shadows older messages in
later projections without deleting them.

## window

A fact that moves the context start forward, optionally with a handoff. It is a
fallback when compaction cannot fit.

## history

The tool that retrieves exact evidence by entry ID or call ID after compaction
or pruning.

## mode

`plan`, `build`, or `act`. A mode selects the default policy for tools and shell
commands.

## rule

A static policy entry in config. Rules can match tool, path prefix, and command
prefix and return allow, deny, or ask.

## grant

A process-local approval created by answering `a`. It matches the same tool and
path or command.

## hook

A configured shell command around a tool call (`before_tool` or `after_tool`).

## skill

A `SKILL.md` body loaded on demand. The request carries a catalog; the `skill`
tool loads the body.

## MCP

Model Context Protocol. Cade Mini runs stdio MCP servers and exposes their tools
as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`.

## subagent

A child run with its own session and a restricted tool set. It cannot spawn
another subagent.

## snapshot

A pre-change copy of a file, used by `--undo` and `/undo`.

## goal

A durable objective in `.cade-mini/goal.json`, separate from the session
schema.

# Testing

<!-- source: design/testing.md -->

# Testing

Tests are grouped by the layer they protect. Run the smallest group that covers
a change, then the full suite before a release.

## Commands

```bash
mkdir -p e2e-results
uv run --locked pytest -q tests --basetemp=e2e-results/pytest
uv run --locked pytest -q tests/test_mini_loop.py --basetemp=e2e-results/pytest
uv run --locked ruff check src/cade_mini/ tests/
uv run --locked ruff format --check src/cade_mini/ tests/
uv run --locked pyright src/cade_mini/
uv run --locked python -m cade_mini.docs check
```

## Coverage map

| Area | Tests |
| --- | --- |
| Sessions | `test_mini_log.py` |
| Projection and pairing | `test_mini_projection.py` |
| Budget, pruning, wire format | `test_mini_request.py` |
| Loop, approvals, retries, windows | `test_mini_loop.py` |
| Provider and auth | `test_mini_provider.py`, `test_mini_auth.py`, `test_mini_siwc_auth.py`, `test_responses_siwc_contract.py` |
| Workspace tools | `test_mini_tools.py` |
| Compaction and windows | `test_mini_compaction.py`, `test_mini_window.py` |
| CLI and config | `test_mini_cli.py`, `test_mini_config.py` |
| Instructions, skills, memory, NOTE | `test_mini_instructions.py`, `test_mini_skills.py`, `test_mini_memory.py`, `test_mini_note.py` |
| Safety and modes | `test_mini_policy.py`, `test_mini_shell.py`, `test_mini_grants.py` |
| Extensions | `test_mini_hooks.py`, `test_mini_mcp.py`, `test_mini_subagents.py` |
| Recovery | `test_mini_snapshots.py`, `test_mini_goal.py` |
| Docs | `test_mini_docs.py` |
| Import firewall | `test_mini_boundary.py` |

## Real-provider checks

The acceptance runs use OpenAI Responses with an API key or ChatGPT plan usage
and are not part of the default test suite. They cover tool use, resume,
compaction, skills, build mode, and write/read. Record the command and observed
result in the change that adds a new acceptance.

## Docs checks

`test_mini_docs.py` and `python -m cade_mini.docs check` validate the manifest,
links, anchors, and generated catalogs. The docs job runs in CI.

## Standalone distribution

Build the wheel and source archive with `uv build --no-sources`. Install the
wheel in a clean virtual environment and check both `cade-mini --help` and
`python -m cade_mini --help` outside the source tree. No Cade package or command
should be present. See the [validation guidelines](../testing.md).

# Cade Mini session schema

<!-- source: reference/session-schema.md -->

# Cade Mini session schema

> Current writer: v2. Readers accept v1 and v2, including mixed-version logs.
> This is the persistent format and projection contract.

## Envelope

One JSON object per line in `session-<id>.jsonl`:

```json
{"v":2,"id":"e2","parent":"e1","ts":"2026-10-18T03:00:00+00:00","type":"user","data":{"text":"Fix the test","source":"user"}}
```

| Field | Type | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v` | `1` or `2` | Read both versions; append v2; reject other values |
| `id` | string | Unique in the file; 12 lowercase hex characters |
| `parent` | string or null | Previous head; null only for the first event |
| `ts` | string | ISO 8601 UTC timestamp |
| `type` | string | One of the event types below |
| `data` | object | Type-specific payload |

The first increment has one active branch: the head is the last event. `parent`
is stored from day one so fork and rewind do not need a schema change.

Unknown event types are a version error. Do not ignore them.

V2 payloads are validated on append and read. Unknown fields, wrong primitive
types, invalid enums, and non-finite numbers are rejected. Missing optional
fields are allowed but defaults are not written into the record. `user.source`
defaults to `user`; assistant model/provider/usage/replay metadata and nullable
artifact/handoff/usage/details fields may be absent. Cross-event call pairing
and context-cut references are validated by projection. V1 keeps legacy reading
rules. Branch copies preserve source event versions.

## Event types

### Conversation events

These produce model-visible messages.

| Type | Payload | Projection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `system` | `{"text": str}` | Latest one is emitted first; never shadowed |
| `user` | `{"text": str, "source": "user"\|"runtime"}` | User message at its position |
| `assistant` | `{"blocks": [Block], "model": str, "provider": str, "usage": object\|null, "provider_state": object\|null}` | Assistant message; empty blocks are skipped |
| `tool_result` | `{"call_id": str, "status": "ok"\|"error"\|"interrupted", "content": str, "artifact": object\|null}` | Tool message; paired with its call |
| `compaction` | `{"summary": str, "first_kept_id": str, "tokens_before": int, "model": str, "provider": str, "usage": object\|null, "details": object\|null}` | Emits a summary message, then the tail from `first_kept_id` |
| `window` | `{"start_id": str, "reason": "manual"\|"fallback", "handoff": str\|null}` | Starts the projection at `start_id`; optional handoff summary |

A block is one of:

```json
{"type":"text","text":"..."}
{"type":"tool_call","id":"c1","name":"bash","args":{"command":"pytest -q"}}
```

`assistant.blocks` is the only record of a tool call. Do not add a separate
`tool_use` event. The `tool_result.call_id` pairs with it.

A `provider_state` is opaque adapter data for Responses replay. It is
stored on the assistant fact and passed back to the same adapter. It never enters
the conversation vocabulary.

### Log-only events

These are recorded but never projected.

| Type | Payload | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `meta` | `{"session": str, "project": str, "created": str}` | First event; identifies the session |
| `request` | `{"model": str, "provider": str, "tools_digest": str, "conversation_digest": str, "context": [str], "estimated_tokens": int, "dropped": [str], "snapshot": object}` | Request audit; v2 adds the normalized snapshot below |
| `run` | `{"termination": str, "steps": int, "usage": object\|null, "error": str\|null}` | Run outcome |
| `attempt` | `{"model": str, "provider": str, "error": str, "usage": object\|null}` | Failed model attempt that produced no message |

The v2 `request.snapshot` contains `messages`, `tools`, `options`, `budget`, and
`report`. `budget` records the context window, output reserve, and headroom;
`report` records the admission result. Options omit API keys, all headers,
cancellation signals, and callbacks. This is the provider-interface input, not
an HTTP capture. The remaining request data is not redacted. A v1 request has no
snapshot; do not infer it from current provider behavior.

A failed attempt does not become an assistant message. A run result does not
duplicate the final answer; the answer is the last assistant text.

## Invariants

1. **One fact, one record.** A tool call appears once, in its assistant event.
   The final answer is not stored again.
2. **No derived content.** No replacement message list, no rendered preview used
   as history, no display summary.
3. **Decisions are facts.** A compaction cut and a window start are logged; the
   messages they produce are recomputed.
4. **Request context is audited, not history.** Dynamic context and the request
   envelope live in `request`; only conversation events project.
5. **A compaction cut is a user turn.** `first_kept_id` must name a `user` event
   before the compaction. A tool call and its result never cross the cut.
6. **A window start is a user turn.** `start_id` must name a `user` event before
   the window.
7. **The latest system event wins.** It is projected first and is not shadowed by
   compaction or a window.

## Projection

`project(branch) -> list[Message]` is pure and deterministic.

1. Find the latest `system` event. Emit it first.
2. Find the latest `window`. If present, start at its `start_id` and keep its
   non-empty `handoff` for a summary message.
3. Find the latest `compaction` at or after the window start. If present, emit
   its summary and start the tail at `first_kept_id`.
4. Walk the retained entries in order. Emit `user`, `assistant`, and
   `tool_result` messages. Skip `system`, `meta`, `window`, `compaction`,
   `request`, `run`, and `attempt`.
5. Pair tool calls with results by call ID.
6. For an open call at the end, synthesize one interrupted result. Do not write
   it to the log. Insert it after the assistant message that contains the call.
7. Reject an orphan result, a duplicate result, a duplicate call, a bad cut, or a
   bad window with `ProjectionError`.

Order of emitted summary messages: system, window handoff, compaction summary,
retained tail.

The wire adapter renders `SummaryMessage` as a user-role message wrapped in
`<compaction-summary>` or `<window-handoff>`. The internal role stays distinct so
hosts can render it differently.

## Storage

- Directory: `.cade-mini/sessions/` by default.
- File: `session-<id>.jsonl`.
- Append lock: `session-<id>.lock`.
- Run lock: `session-<id>.run.lock`; concurrent turns are rejected.
- Append: one line, `flush`, `fsync`.
- Before append: truncate an incomplete trailing line from a crash.
- On read: ignore an incomplete trailing line; reject any earlier invalid line.
- Reject duplicate IDs and forward parent references.
- No rewrite, no in-place edit.

## Compaction record

```json
{"v":2,"id":"e80","parent":"e79","ts":"...","type":"compaction",
 "data":{"summary":"## Goal\n...","first_kept_id":"e52","tokens_before":48210,
         "model":"gpt-5.6-luna","provider":"chatgpt",
         "usage":{"input":43000,"output":1200},"details":null}}
```

The summary is model-generated content and must be logged. The original events
before `first_kept_id` stay in the log. A later compaction starts after the
previous one and may include the previous summary in its input.

## Window record

```json
{"v":2,"id":"e90","parent":"e89","ts":"...","type":"window",
 "data":{"start_id":"e88","reason":"manual","handoff":"Optional note."}}
```

A window is the hard fallback. Compaction is the default. A window is explicit
through `/new-context`, or automatic when compaction cannot reduce enough.

## Versioning

`v` is the only compatibility switch. A change to an existing payload, a new
conversation event type, or a change to projection semantics requires a new `v`
and a migration note. Adding a log-only event type is a new `v` as well, because
older readers must reject it rather than ignore it. See the
[upgrade guide](../upgrade/README.md) for v1 resume and rollback.

# Subsystems

<!-- source: subsystems/README.md -->

# Subsystems

Each page owns one subsystem's types, behavior, and failure modes. The
[architecture](../architecture.md) is the map; these pages are the reference.

- [Log](log.md): append, lock, branch, list, and repair.
- [Projection and request](projection-request.md): deterministic context and
  budget admission.
- [Loop](loop.md): provider calls, tools, approvals, retries, and facts.
- [Tools and policy](tools-policy.md): workspace tools, modes, rules, grants,
  shell classification, approvals.
- [Context and compaction](context-compaction.md): summaries, windows, history,
  and request context.
- [Extensions](extensions.md): skills, memory, hooks, MCP, subagents, snapshots,
  goals, and hosts.

A subsystem page describes current behavior. Historical decisions belong in
[decision records](../decisions/README.md) and incidents in
[postmortems](../postmortem/README.md).

# Log

<!-- source: subsystems/log.md -->

# Log

`SessionLog` owns the append-only JSONL file.

## Create and open

- `SessionLog.create(directory, session_id=None)` creates a unique file and
  writes a `meta` entry.
- `SessionLog.open(path)` validates the envelope and v2 payloads. Reads ignore a
  torn final line; the next valid append truncates that tail.
- The session ID is derived from the file name when not supplied.

## Append

`append(type, data)`:

1. Validates the v2 payload without modifying the file.
2. Takes an exclusive file lock.
3. Repairs a torn tail and reads the current entries to get the parent ID.
4. Builds an entry with ID, timestamp, parent, type, and data.
5. Appends one JSON line, flushes, and calls `fsync`.
6. Releases the lock.

`fsync` is deliberate: a returned append is durable enough to resume. A failed
write raises `LogError` and does not return a fake entry.

`run_lock()` protects a whole turn separately from individual appends. It rejects
competing operations immediately with `LogError`. `run()` and manual CLI context
changes use it; other multi-event storage clients must acquire it explicitly.

## Branch

`branch()` follows parent IDs from the last entry back to the root and reverses
the list. It rejects cycles, missing parents, and duplicate IDs.

## Listing and titles

`list_sessions(directory)` returns session ID, update time, and a title derived
from the first user text. Corrupt files are skipped so one bad session cannot
break the list.

## Invariants

- Entries are never rewritten in place.
- IDs are unique within a file.
- A parent precedes its child.
- The file ends with exactly one newline.
- The schema version is closed; new event types require a decision record.

## Tests

`test_mini_log.py` covers create, append, resume, tail repair, branching, and
listing. `test_mini_projection.py` covers malformed branches.

# Projection and request

<!-- source: subsystems/projection-request.md -->

# Projection and request

## Projection

`project(entries)` is pure. It:

1. Finds the latest `system` entry.
2. Applies the latest `window` start.
3. Applies the latest `compaction` cut and emits a summary message.
4. Converts user, assistant, and tool-result facts to messages.
5. Pairs each tool call with its result by call ID.
6. Inserts a synthetic interrupted result if the branch ends inside a call.

It rejects orphan results, duplicate results, and cuts that do not point to a
user entry. The projection does not call a provider or write the log.

## Request

`build(conversation, tools, budget, context)`:

1. Joins the base system prompt with request-only context.
2. Estimates tokens.
3. Preserves all projected messages and tool bodies.
4. Converts to provider messages and tool definitions.
5. Returns a `Request` and a `BuildReport`.

`BuildReport` records estimated tokens and budget. Legacy dropped-call and
turn counters remain empty/zero. `require_sendable()` raises `RequestTooLarge`
when the full request cannot fit. The loop reduces context only through logged
compaction and window decisions, then rejects any remaining overflow.

## Context order

The system message carries base instructions plus, in order: instructions,
skill catalog, NOTE, memory, and goal. These inputs are request-only; the
v2 request audit records their full text, the admitted messages, tool definitions,
non-authentication options, and budget. Session files can contain sensitive input.

## Tests

`test_mini_projection.py`, `test_mini_request.py`, and
`test_mini_compaction.py` cover cuts, strict admission, and wire-format contracts.

# Loop

<!-- source: subsystems/loop.md -->

# Loop

`run(log, text, ...)` is the only stage that writes during a turn.

## One run

1. Append the `user` fact.
2. For each step:
   - Project the branch.
   - If the full estimate exceeds budget, call the compactor.
   - Build the request.
   - If still over, call the window fallback.
   - Append a `request` audit fact.
   - Stream the provider.
   - Append the assistant fact.
   - Resolve and execute each tool call.
   - Append tool-result facts.
3. Append one `run` fact with termination, steps, usage, and error.

## Provider handling

The loop collects text deltas, tool calls, usage, and provider replay state. A
failure becomes an `attempt` fact. Retryable failures are retried once by
default; the retry delay is configurable. A terminal failure ends the run with
`provider_error` and never creates an assistant fact.

## Termination

- `completed`: the provider ended without tool calls.
- `step_limit`: the configured step count was reached.
- `context_error`: no request fits after compaction and window fallback.
- `aborted`: cancellation was requested.
- `provider_error`: the provider failed.

## Cancellation

A cancellation token is checked between steps and tool calls. Running tools get
the token; remaining calls receive interrupted results. The run records the
reason in its `run` fact.

## Events

The host receives text deltas, tool start, tool end, and final output. Events are
presentation; facts are durable. A host can drop events without losing history.

## Tests

`test_mini_loop.py` covers completion, tool use, approvals, retries, timeouts,
cancellation, context errors, and window fallback.

# Tools and policy

<!-- source: subsystems/tools-policy.md -->

# Tools and policy

## Tool contract

A tool has a name, description, JSON parameter schema, and async execute. Results
carry content, an error flag, and optional metadata. The loop records results; a
tool never appends to the log.

## Built-in tools

- Workspace: `read`, `write`, `edit`, `glob`, `grep`, `bash`.
- Evidence and context: `history`, `skill`, `memory`, `goal`.
- Delegation: `subagent`.
- Remote: `mcp__<server>__<tool>`.

`write` and `edit` snapshot the target before changing it. `bash` snapshots
common single-command mutation targets.

## Policy

`WorkspacePolicy.check` returns allow, deny, or ask.

Hard checks run first:

- `read` and file writes must stay inside the workspace.
- `bash` workdir must stay inside the workspace.
- Unknown tools are denied.
- `read_only` denies writes, edits, shell, memory, and MCP.

Then:

1. A matching static rule decides.
2. A matching session grant allows.
3. The mode default decides.

Modes:

- `plan`: read tools and read-only shell; writes and mutations denied.
- `build`: writes allowed; read-only shell allowed; mutating shell asks.
- `act`: writes and shell ask.

## Shell classification

`classify_command` labels a command read-only, mutating, or unknown. Pipelines,
redirections, command lists, substitutions, and unknown binaries are unknown.
Plan mode denies unknown; build asks; act asks.

## Grants

`GrantStore` records a path or command for the exact tool. A grant is
process-local. `/permissions` lists and clears it. Durable policy belongs in
rules.

## Approvals

The host resolves ask. `SessionApprover` prompts a TTY with yes/no/always.
`AutoReviewer` makes one tool-free model call and requires an `ALLOW` prefix.
Non-interactive hosts deny unless `--yes` or a rule allows.

## Process isolation

There is no OS sandbox. Shell commands run with the Cade Mini process
permissions. The path boundary, mode, shell classification, and approvals are
the safety layer.

## Tests

`test_mini_tools.py`, `test_mini_policy.py`, `test_mini_grants.py`, and
`test_mini_shell.py`.

# Context and compaction

<!-- source: subsystems/context-compaction.md -->

# Context and compaction

## Request context

The system message is the base prompt plus request-only context:

1. Project instructions from `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or variants.
2. Skill catalog names and descriptions.
3. `NOTE.md` working state.
4. `MEMORY.md` durable facts.
5. An active goal.

The request audit records this context and the normalized request; it does not
turn the text into conversation facts.

## Compaction

`Compactor` runs when the full projection exceeds the input budget.

1. Select the cut at a user boundary that keeps the recent tail under the
   configured target.
2. Serialize older messages, including a prior summary.
3. Ask the provider for a summary with a bounded output.
4. Append a `compaction` fact with summary and `first_kept_id`.
5. Reproject.

A summary failure or a cut with no messages appends an `attempt` fact and leaves
the conversation unchanged. A prior summary is included as `PRIOR SUMMARY`, so
compaction is iterative.

## Window fallback

If compaction cannot fit, the loop may call the window hook. The CLI starts a
window at the latest user entry with a fixed handoff that points to `NOTE.md`
and history. If the request still does not fit, the run terminates with
`context_error`.

## History

The `history` tool searches the branch or reads an exact entry or tool result.
It retrieves evidence outside the current compaction or window boundary.
Exact content is capped; search results point to entry IDs.

## Request admission

Admission preserves the full projection. Overflow requires a logged context
transition or fails with `context_error`. See
[Projection and request](projection-request.md).

## Tests

`test_mini_compaction.py`, `test_mini_window.py`, `test_mini_history.py`, and
the request tests cover cuts, summaries, fallback, and retrieval.

# Extensions

<!-- source: subsystems/extensions.md -->

# Extensions

Extensions add behavior through narrow seams. None changes the session schema.

## Skills

Discovery reads `SKILL.md` from user and project roots. The request carries a
catalog; the `skill` tool loads a body into a tool result. A body is a fact, not
request-only context.

## Memory

`MEMORY.md` is request context. The `memory` tool appends one bullet and cannot
write other paths. The file is capped to protect the request budget.

## Hooks

`HookRunner` executes configured shell commands around tools. `before_tool` can
deny; `after_tool` observes. Hooks are trusted and time-bounded. See
[Hooks, MCP, and subagents](../hooks-mcp-subagents.md).

## MCP

Each configured stdio server keeps one persistent process. Discovery reads
`tools/list`; calls use `tools/call` over a serialized queue. Tools are prefixed
`mcp__`, ask by default, and are denied in plan and read-only modes. A server
that cannot start is reported and skipped.

## Subagents

`SubagentTool` creates a child session under `<sessions>/subagents`. The child
gets the parent provider, budget, policy, approver, hooks, context, and base
tools plus its own history. It cannot spawn another subagent and is limited to
20 steps. The parent records only the call and summary. `DelegateTool` runs one
or more child tasks sequentially and optionally applies a child mode.

## Snapshots

`SnapshotStore` captures `write`, `edit`, and common single-command shell
mutations. `--undo` and `/undo` restore the latest snapshot. Snapshots are project
state, not session facts.

## Goals

`GoalStore` persists one objective in `.cade-mini/goal.json`. The `goal` tool and
`/goal` command manage it. An active goal is request context.

## Hosts

The CLI runs one-shot and REPL sessions. It uses the same loop and policy as
every other entry path.

## Limits

Extensions are deliberately small. MCP is a stdio client, not a full capability
negotiation implementation. Hooks are shell commands, not in-process callbacks.
Subagents are sequential and share the parent approval context.

## Tests

`test_mini_skills.py`, `test_mini_memory.py`, `test_mini_hooks.py`,
`test_mini_mcp.py`, `test_mini_subagents.py`, `test_mini_snapshots.py`, and `test_mini_goal.py`.

# Tools and security

<!-- source: tools-security.md -->

# Tools and security

## Workspace tools

- `read`: read a UTF-8 file with line numbers. Files are capped.
- `write`: write UTF-8 text and create parent directories.
- `edit`: replace one exact occurrence of old text.
- `glob`: list files matching a workspace glob.
- `grep`: search file contents with a regular expression.
- `bash`: run a shell command in the workspace.

## Context and extension tools

- `history`: retrieve evidence outside the current context boundary.
- `skill`: load the full body of an available `SKILL.md`.
- `memory`: append a durable fact to `MEMORY.md`.
- `goal`: read, set, complete, or clear the workspace goal.
- `subagent`: run one child task in its own session.
- `delegate`: run one or more child tasks sequentially, optionally in a mode.
- `mcp__<server>__<tool>`: tools discovered from a configured MCP server.

## Modes

`plan` exposes read, glob, grep, history, skill, and bash. Writes and edits are
hidden and denied. Only classified read-only shell commands are allowed.

`build` exposes all tools. Writes and edits are allowed. Read-only shell
commands are allowed; mutating or unknown commands ask.

`act` exposes all tools. Writes, edits, and shell commands ask.

`--read-only` denies writes, edits, shell commands, memory, and MCP regardless of
mode. It does not block reads, search, history, skills, or goal state.

## Rules and grants

Static rules live in `cade-mini.json`. They are evaluated last match first and
can match tool, path prefix, and command prefix. A hard path boundary always
wins.

A session grant is created when an approval answer is `a` (always). The grant
matches the same tool and the same path or command. `/permissions` lists grants;
`/permissions clear` removes them. Grants last for the process only. Use rules
for durable policy.

## Shell classification

The shell analyzer labels a command as `read_only`, `mutating`, or `unknown`.
It is deliberately conservative:

- `ls`, `cat`, `grep`, `rg`, `git status`, `git diff`, and similar commands are
  read-only.
- `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `git commit`, `python`, and other mutating commands are
  mutating.
- Pipelines, redirections, command lists, substitutions, and unknown binaries
  are unknown.

Plan mode denies unknown commands. Build and act ask.

## Approvals

An ask is answered by:

- `--yes`: approve.
- `--auto-review`: ask the model for `ALLOW` or `DENY`; failures deny.
- Otherwise a TTY prompt: `y` once, `n` deny, `a` always for this exact call.
- Non-TTY without `--yes` or auto-review: deny.

## Process isolation

Cade Mini does not implement an OS sandbox. `bash` runs with the permissions of
the Cade Mini process. The path boundary, modes, shell classification, and
approvals are the safety layer; do not run untrusted commands or repositories
with `--yes`.

## Best practices

- Use `plan` for review and `build` for scoped edits.
- Prefer explicit rules over `--yes` in shared repositories.
- Keep commands simple so the classifier can reason about them.
- Use `--read-only` for inspection-only automation.

# Snapshots and goals

<!-- source: snapshots-goals.md -->

# Snapshots and goals

## File snapshots

Cade Mini records a snapshot before a file tool changes a file. Snapshots live
under `.cade-mini/snapshots` with a JSONL index and one directory per snapshot.

Covered changes:

- `write` and `edit`.
- Common single-command shell mutations: `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `touch`, `mkdir`,
  redirection with `>`, and `sed -i`.
- Creating a file records that it did not exist; undo removes it.

Not covered:

- Complex pipelines, command lists, unknown scripts, and commands that mutate
  files without naming them.
- Files larger than the snapshot limit (5 MiB) are rejected rather than
  silently skipped.
- Directory trees are not copied; directory mutations are skipped.

## Undo

```bash
cade-mini --undo
```

This restores the latest snapshot and exits without contacting a provider. In
the REPL, use `/undo`. Each call restores one snapshot, so repeated undo walks
back through the recorded changes. Stop external file writers before undo.

Undo checks that the current file matches the recorded post-change state. It
rejects conflicts, corrupt payloads, and snapshots whose outcome is unknown.
A rejected undo leaves the file and index unchanged. Legacy snapshots have no
post-change state and require manual inspection; automatic undo rejects them.

Snapshots are project state, not session facts. They are not part of the
JSONL session branch.

## Goals

A goal is one durable objective stored in `.cade-mini/goal.json`. It has an
objective, a status (`active` or `done`), and an update time.

```bash
cade-mini --goal "Add a regression test for the parser" "Start the task."
```

In the REPL:

- `/goal` shows the current goal.
- `/goal TEXT` sets an active goal.
- `/goal done` marks it complete.
- `/goal clear` removes it.

The `goal` tool provides the same actions to the model. An active goal is added
to request context so a resumed or compacted session still knows the objective.
Goals are host state; they do not change the session schema.

Goals are intentionally small. Use `NOTE.md` for working details and `MEMORY.md`
for facts that outlive the objective.

# Skills and memory

<!-- source: skills-memory.md -->

# Skills and memory

## Skills

Cade Mini discovers `SKILL.md` files in two roots:

1. `~/.cade-mini/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` for user skills.
2. `<project>/.cade-mini/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` for project skills.

Later roots override earlier roots with the same skill name. A skill file can
start with YAML frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: release-check
description: Validate release metadata before tagging.
---

Run the release checklist...
```

`name` defaults to the parent directory. `description` defaults to the first
non-empty body line. Invalid names and empty bodies are skipped.

The request gets a compact `<available-skills>` catalog with names and
descriptions. The model loads a body on demand with the `skill` tool:

```json
{"name": "release-check"}
```

Skill bodies are facts in the tool result, not request-only context. Loading the
same skill twice is harmless but adds another tool result.

## Memory

`MEMORY.md` at the project root stores durable facts. It is loaded into request
context as `<memory source="MEMORY.md">` on every task, capped at 32 KiB.

The model appends facts with the `memory` tool:

```json
{"text": "Prefer pytest and keep changes minimal."}
```

`memory` writes only `MEMORY.md`; it cannot write arbitrary paths. The file is
capped at 64 KiB for writes. Remove stale entries manually when it fills.

Memory is different from the other state files:

- `AGENTS.md` is project instruction, owned by the project.
- `NOTE.md` is short-lived working state; it is summarized with compaction.
- `MEMORY.md` is a durable preference or convention.
- The session log is the record of what happened.

## Request context

Instructions, skill catalog, `NOTE.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and an active goal are all
request-only context. They appear in each request audit but never become
conversation messages. See [Sessions and context](sessions-context.md).

# Hooks, MCP, and subagents

<!-- source: hooks-mcp-subagents.md -->

# Hooks, MCP, and subagents

## Hooks

Hooks run shell commands around tools. They are configured in `cade-mini.json`:

```json
{
  "hooks": [
    {
      "event": "before_tool",
      "command": "python tools/check_tool.py",
      "matcher": "bash",
      "timeout_ms": 10000
    }
  ]
}
```

- `before_tool` runs after policy and approval, before the tool executes. A
